l: pride, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: Pride is associated with senseless discussion and excessive opinion of oneself. It is destroyed through the Word and devotion to God's name.

l: saints, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: The saints please God's heart, adorn God's gate, and hymn God's praises. Those who are outside God's favour do not enter and wander in many births.

l: caste, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: The speaker identifies himself as a singer of low caste while others call themselves of high caste. The unit contrasts these caste claims with devotion to God.

l: meditation on the True One, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: Those who meditate on God are the people from whom the speaker begs. Meditation on God is presented alongside devotion rather than claims of high caste.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok X .. Pauri X
s: Guru Nanak teaches that worldly rulers, possessions, relationships, beauty, sweetness, and the whole world are false and pass away, while only God is wholly true. He explains that man becomes true through truth in the heart, love for the True One, knowledge of the true way, mercy, charity, and instruction from the true Guru. Truth is described as medicine that removes sin, and man is urged to seek the dust of the saints' feet, abandon false covetousness, meditate on the Unseen One, and serve according to his allotted reward.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok X .. Pauri X
s: Guru Nanak teaches that worldly things and the whole world are false except God. He explains how man becomes true through truth, love for the True One, mercy, charity, and instruction from the true Guru.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok X .. Pauri X
s: God is described as the only reality that is not false. Man forgets the Creator when he loves false things.

l: man, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok X .. Pauri X
s: Man becomes true when truth is in his heart, falsehood departs, and he loves the True One. He is urged to know the true way, show mercy, perform charity, seek instruction from the true Guru, meditate on the Unseen One, and serve according to what has been allotted.

l: world, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok X .. Pauri X
s: The whole world is described as false and passing away. Its rulers, subjects, dwellings, possessions, relationships, beauty, sweetness, and wealth are all said to be false.

l: falsehood, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok X .. Pauri X
s: Falsehood causes man to love what is false and forget the Creator. It is associated with covetousness, and its removal cleanses man and washes away sin.

l: truth, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok X .. Pauri X
s: Truth in the heart makes man true and leads him toward salvation. Truth is called medicine for all because it removes and washes away sin.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Guru Nanak describes an age in which truth is scarce, falsehood prevails, and greed, sin, and lust govern society. He teaches that the whole seed of the Name germinates, and that fear, modesty, and devotion can remove falsehood from a person. He says that man's evil is seen by the True One, that human effort succeeds only through what the Creator does, and that caste has no power in the next world. In Pauri XI, God is said to create the different worlds, unite some beings with Himself, lead others astray, and reveal Himself through the favour of the Guru.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Guru Nanak teaches that truth is scarce and falsehood prevails in the age. He describes the corruption of rulers, priests, religious pretenders, and ordinary people, and states that honour will properly weigh a person. He also says that man's evil is seen by the True One and that caste has no power in the next world.

l: truth, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Truth is described as being in dearth during the age.

l: falsehood, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Falsehood prevails in the age and is described as master of the mint. Guru Nanak says that devotion can remove every trace of falsehood from a person.

l: God's name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Those who have sown the seed of the Name depart with honour.

l: seed of the Name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: The seed of the Name must be whole to germinate in the proper season; half-seed cannot germinate.

l: devotion, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Devotion is used to dye the body after fear has been placed in the vat and modesty made its base. Through devotion, no trace of falsehood remains.

l: greed, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Greed and sin rule as ruler and village accountant. Subjects satisfy the judge's greed with bribes, and fools amass wealth through tricks and cavilling.

l: sin, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Sin is described with greed as ruler and village accountant in the corrupt age.

l: lust, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Lust is the minister who summons and examines people and sits in judgement over them.

l: salvation, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Pretended religious men spoil their religious acts while still wanting the door of salvation. Those who leave their homes and call themselves continent do not know the way.

l: man's evil, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Man's evil becomes known, and the True One sees all.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: God creates the different worlds. God blends some beings with Himself and leads others astray from Him.

l: caste, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Caste has no power in the next world, where there is a new order of beings.

l: animals, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: Creatures have nothing in their own power; God creates the different worlds and determines what takes place.

l: world, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: The different worlds are created by God.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XI .. Pauri XI
s: The Guru's favour enables God to be known, because through the Guru God reveals Himself.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XII .. Pauri XII
s: Guru Nanak teaches that pain can serve as medicine while worldly pleasure is a disease that turns people from God. He praises God as the Doer whose light fills all creation and says that uttering divine praise brings salvation. Guru Angad teaches that repeating the name of the one God is the highest duty, above the duties of different social groups. Guru Nanak and Guru Angad both connect divine knowledge with understanding God and the soul, while Guru Nanak says that divine knowledge requires a guru. The unit also teaches that both literate and illiterate people will be judged according to their actions.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XII .. Pauri XII
s: Guru Nanak teaches that pain is medicine and worldly pleasure is a disease, and he declares that God is the Doer while he does nothing. He praises God’s omnipotence and says that God’s light pervades and contains all creatures. He also says that divine knowledge restrains the mind and cannot be obtained without a guru.

l: Guru Angad, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XII .. Pauri XII
s: Guru Angad teaches that repeating the name of the one God is the highest duty, above the duties associated with Jogis, Brahmans, Khatris, and Sudars. He says that one who knows the secret of this is a bright God himself, and that Nanak is his slave. He also describes God as the Supreme God of souls and says that one who knows the secrets of the soul and God is a bright God himself.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XII .. Pauri XII
s: God is described as the Doer, omnipotent, and without a visible end. God’s light pervades creatures and contains them, filling both inanimate and animate creation. God’s praise is beautiful, and the person who utters it is saved.

l: worldly pleasure, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XII .. Pauri XII
s: Worldly pleasure is described as a disease. Where worldly pleasure exists, there is no desire for God.

l: divine knowledge, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XII .. Pauri XII
s: Divine knowledge controls and restrains the mind. The text says that divine knowledge cannot exist without a guru.

l: God's name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XII .. Pauri XII
s: The name of the one God is presented as the highest duty for all, above the duties assigned to different social groups. One who knows its secret is described as a bright God himself.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XII .. Pauri XII
s: A guru is necessary for divine knowledge to exist. Without a guru, the mind cannot be restrained by divine knowledge.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: Guru Nanak teaches that the body and its guiding qualities change across the four ages, with passion and falsehood characterizing the Kal age. He describes what the four Veds say about the Lord, God's name, truth, and the Kal age, and says that love, devotion, and humility lead to salvation. He declares himself devoted to the true Guru, who teaches divine instruction, enables the sight of God in the world, and mercifully saves those who recognize him as a boat. Those who abandon the Lord for mammon are wrecked.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: Guru Nanak teaches about the changing qualities of the body and its driver in each age. He explains what the four Veds state and says that love, devotion, and humility lead to salvation. He declares himself a sacrifice to the true Guru.

l: Kal age, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: In the Kal age, passion is the carriage and falsehood is the driver in front. The Atharv belongs to this age, when God's name was called Allah, men wore blue clothes, and Turks and Pathans ruled.

l: truth, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: Truth is described as the quality desired and lived in during the Sat age. In the Dwapar age, truth was the driver in front.

l: Veds, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: The four Veds are described as true according to the Hindus, but reading and studying them reveals four different doctrines. They state different teachings about the Lord, God's name, truth, and the Kal age.

l: Lord, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: The Lord is described in the Sam Ved as white-robed, with men desiring and abiding in truth. Those who leave the Lord and attach themselves to mammon are wrecked.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: God is said to be beheld in the world through the true Guru's divine instruction. The Rig is said to describe God's name as everywhere contained and as the sun in heaven.

l: God's name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: God's name is described as present everywhere and like the sun in heaven. Repeating it causes sins to depart and enables man to obtain salvation; in the Kal age it was called Allah.

l: salvation, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: Salvation is obtained when man has love and devotion and is himself lowly. The Rig also says that repeating God's name leads man to salvation.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIII .. Pauri XIII
s: The true Guru gives divine instruction through which God is seen in the world. He is a boat, and he mercifully saves those who recognize him as such.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: Guru Nanak teaches that outward greatness, ritual, and bowing are worthless without inner purity and the guidance of the true Guru. The simmal-tree of the desert disappoints birds because its fruit, flowers, and leaves are useless, while a lowly tree with sweet fruit has exquisite qualities. He warns that the wicked man may bow repeatedly while retaining an impure heart, and that people must leave their beauty and possessions behind and face the results of their good and bad deeds. The dead must travel the narrow road, may be sent naked to hell, and will regret their sins.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: Guru Nanak teaches that outward rituals, arguments, worship of stones, falsehoods, and religious markings are vain without knowledge of God's designs and guidance from the true Guru. He also teaches that inner purity matters more than repeated bowing and that people must face the results of their deeds.

l: simmal-tree of the desert, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: The simmal-tree of the desert is very tall and thick, but birds that approach it with hope leave disappointed because its fruit is insipid, its flowers are unwholesome, and its leaves are useless.

l: wicked man, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: The wicked man bows twice more than anyone else, but his repeated bowing is of no avail if his heart is impure.

l: vain religion, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: The vain religion consists of outward practices such as reading books, performing twilight devotions, arguing, worshipping stones, sitting like cranes, uttering falsehoods, meditating on the Gayatri, and wearing religious marks and garments. Guru Nanak says that without the true Guru, this religion does not provide the way.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: The true Guru is necessary for finding the way. Without the true Guru, a person will not find the way.

l: good and bad deeds, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: A person obtains the fruit of the good or bad deeds that person has done. Sovereignty and worldly success do not prevent the person from proceeding by the narrow road.

l: hell, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: A person may be sent naked to hell, which will then appear very formidable.

l: sins, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIV .. Pauri XIV
s: A person will regret the sins committed after leaving earthly raiment and pleasing beauty behind and facing what follows.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: Slok XV teaches that a true janeu is made of mercy, contentment, continence, and truth, and that it does not break, soil, burn, or get lost. Guru Nanak contrasts this spiritual thread with the purchased cotton janeu, which falls away at death and does not restrain theft, adultery, falsehood, abuse, or other wrongdoing. Guru Nanak says that adoring and praising the Name gives honour and a true thread fit for God's court, while criticizing the absence of moral strings for the body and senses. Pauri XV teaches that the Lord's compassion leads a person to do the Master's work, obey God's order, reach God's court, and receive the desired fruit and a robe of honour.

l: Slok XV, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: Slok XV teaches that mercy, contentment, continence, and truth form a lasting janeu for the soul. It contrasts this spiritual thread with the external cotton janeu and describes its failure at death.

l: Pauri XV, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: Pauri XV teaches that a person whom the Lord treats compassionately will do the Master's work and worship according to God's order. Such a person reaches God's court, receives the fruit desired by the heart, and is clothed with a robe of honour.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: Guru Nanak teaches that a true janeu consists of mercy, contentment, continence, and truth, and that praising the Name gives honour and a thread fit for God's court. He criticizes the purchased cotton janeu, which does not prevent wrongdoing, falls away at death, and is accompanied by external rituals and mental blindness.

l: the Brahman, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: The Brahman purchases and puts on a cotton janeu, whispers that the Brahman is the guru of the Hindus, and later twists strings for the neck and puts them on others. The Brahman takes hire for marrying and shows a paper about the fate of a wedded pair, while wandering astray without moral strings.

l: janeu, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: The janeu is described in two forms: a lasting spiritual thread made from mercy, contentment, continence, and truth, and a purchased cotton thread put on in a ceremony. The cotton janeu becomes old, is thrown away, and falls when a person dies, while the true thread does not break or become soiled, burned, or lost.

l: soul, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: The soul is to receive a janeu made of mercy, contentment, continence, and truth. At death, the external janeu falls while the soul departs without it.

l: Lord, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: The Lord is compassionate and merciful toward the worshipper whom He causes to abide by His order. Through the Lord's compassion, that person does the Master's work and worships Him.

l: divine order, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: God's order is the rule by which the worshipper abides and worships the Lord. Obeying God's order makes a person acceptable and leads that person toward God's court.

l: God's court, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XV .. Pauri XV
s: God's court is the place where the person who obeys the Master's order reaches, receives the fruit desired by the heart, and is clothed with a robe of honour. The true spiritual thread is described as fit for entrance into God's court.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVI .. Pauri XVI
s: The unit concerns hypocrisy in religious practice, especially among those who wear Hindu marks and rosaries while eating the bread of malechhas and associating with Muhammadans. Guru Nanak condemns false dealings, ritual defilement, and violence, and urges meditation on the True One. It teaches that God sees all, assigns duties, bestows greatness, and can reduce monarchs to poverty.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVI .. Pauri XVI
s: Guru Nanak condemns hypocrisy, falsehood, violence, and empty ritual observance. He urges people to repeat God's name and meditate on the True One.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVI .. Pauri XVI
s: God sees all, moves people beneath His glance, bestows greatness, and causes people to do good works. He assigns people their duties and can reduce monarchs to poverty.

l: Brahmans, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVI .. Pauri XVI
s: Brahmans sound shells, perform Hindu worship, and enjoy viands, but the text calls their capital and dealings false. They wear sacrificial marks and reddish dhotis, carry knives, and maintain strict cooking boundaries while their bodies, actions, and hearts are described as defiled or false.

l: Muhammadans, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVI .. Pauri XVI
s: Muhammadans are associated with by those who publicly read the Quran while performing Hindu worship at home. Their court accepts people wearing blue clothes, and those people take bread from malechhas while worshipping the Purans.

l: malechhas, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVI .. Pauri XVI
s: Malechhas provide bread that some people eat while maintaining Hindu ritual practices. The text also describes people as taking bread from malechhas while seeking acceptance in the Muhammadans' court.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVII .. Pauri XVII
s: The unit concerns the consequences of dishonest offerings, truthful purity, and the failure of worldly people who forget God. It says that ancestors receiving stolen offerings will be known as thieves, and that only earnings gained through work will benefit a person in the next world. Guru Nanak teaches that falsehood is despised and that true purity comes from having God in the heart. It describes men who enjoy adorned women, grand dwellings, and authority but forget death and ultimately fail when old age comes.

l: ancestors, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVII .. Pauri XVII
s: The ancestors who receive the fruits of a robber’s theft will be known in the next world as thieves.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVII .. Pauri XVII
s: God does justice by cutting off the hand of the Brahman go-between. God is said to dwell in the heart of the truly pure, while those who do not know God fail.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVII .. Pauri XVII
s: Guru Nanak teaches that only the fruit of a person’s earnings and toil will be obtained in the next world. He also teaches that true purity comes from having God in the heart.

l: falsehood, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVII .. Pauri XVII
s: Falsehood dwells in the mouth of the false person, who is ever despised.

l: adorned women, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVII .. Pauri XVII
s: Adorned women are among the pleasures and displays on which men fix their hearts. Men behold their women’s chambers and forget death.

l: men, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVII .. Pauri XVII
s: Men fix their hearts on caparisoned horses and adorned women, live in mansions, pavilions, and palaces, and enjoy pleasures. They exercise authority and forget death, but they fail because they do not know God, and their youth will fail when old age comes.

l: Death, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVII .. Pauri XVII
s: Death is forgotten by men who behold their women’s chambers and enjoy worldly authority and pleasure. The unit says that old age will come and youth will fail them.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVIII .. Pauri XVIII
s: The unit concerns impurity, divine knowledge, God, Guru Nanak, and the True Guru. It teaches that impurity is present in everything if judged by physical contamination, but that impurity is truly rooted in greed, falsehood, coveting, slander, superstition, and worldly attachment. Guru Nanak states that divine knowledge washes away impurity and that those who know God have no impurity. The True Guru leads people to behold God's greatness, brings God's praises into the heart, removes evil, and grants the nine treasures when God is pleased.

l: impurity, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVIII .. Pauri XVIII
s: Impurity is said to be present in everything if physical contamination is admitted, including water, kitchens, cow-dung, wood, and grain. Its deeper forms are greed, falsehood, gazing on another's wealth or wife, listening to slander, superstition, and attachment to worldly things.

l: divine knowledge, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVIII .. Pauri XVIII
s: Divine knowledge washes away impurity rather than physical washing.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVIII .. Pauri XVIII
s: God ordains birth and death and sends sustenance through eating and drinking, which are described as pure. When God is pleased, the nine treasures are obtained, and those who know God have no impurity.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVIII .. Pauri XVIII
s: Guru Nanak teaches that impurity is not washed away by physical means but by divine knowledge. He also states that pretended saints who practice greed, falsehood, coveting, or slander shall go bound to hell.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XVIII .. Pauri XVIII
s: The True Guru possesses all greatness and can cause people to meet God and behold His greatness. If the True Guru is pleased, he causes God's praises to dwell in the heart, removes evil from within, and, when God is pleased, the nine treasures are obtained.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: The unit describes the Brahman purifying himself, preparing sacred food, and reciting Sanskrit verses while eating. It teaches that food becomes impure when it enters a sinful body, and that a mouth which eats without uttering the Name is like something spat upon. Guru Nanak explains that people depend on a vessel throughout life, while only the True God is independent of a vessel. Pauri XIX teaches that each person bears the result of their own acts, should avoid pride, call no one bad, and not dispute with a fool.

l: the Brahman, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: The Brahman purifies himself, sits in a purified square, receives purified food that no one may touch, and eats while reading Sanskrit verses.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: Guru Nanak teaches that people depend on a vessel for conception, birth, marriage, friendship, worldly life, and replacement after death. He says that only the True God is independent of a vessel and that the face praising Him will be bright in His court.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: The True God is the only one independent of a vessel. Those who praise Him are described as fortunate and beautiful, and their faces will be bright in His court.

l: food, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: The food is made holy when ghi is added to holy corn, water, fire, and salt. It becomes impure when it enters a sinful body, as if spat upon.

l: the true Name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: The Name is what the mouth should utter while eating. A mouth that does not utter the Name, even while eating delicacies, is considered as if spat upon.

l: vessel, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: A vessel is involved in a person's conception, birth, marriage, friendships, worldly passage, and attachment. When one vessel dies, another is sought, and a vessel gives rise to another vessel.

l: acts and accountability, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: Every person must bear the result of their own acts and adjust their own account.

l: pride, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XIX .. Pauri XIX
s: Pauri XIX asks why people practise pride when they are not to remain in this world.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XX .. Pauri XX
s: Guru Nanak teaches that evil people are rejected and punished in God's court, while good people devote themselves to God. Those who are inwardly foul remain impure despite ritual bathing, whereas those who love God may weep, laugh, or remain silent in devotion. God created the world, governs its changes, and will judge the accounts of the wicked. Everyone must eventually depart, so people should arrange their affairs with God in mind.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XX .. Pauri XX
s: Guru Nanak teaches that evil people are foolish, rejected in God's court, and punished. He also describes the devotion of good people and the judgment awaiting the wicked.

l: Lord, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XX .. Pauri XX
s: God is the true Master whom good people love, contemplate, and obey. God created the world, infused it with power, observes its changes, and judges the accounts of the wicked.

l: evil person, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XX .. Pauri XX
s: The evil person is evil in mind, body, and reputation, and is rejected in God's court. The evil person is described as foolish, spat upon, and punished with shoe-beatings.

l: good people, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XX .. Pauri XX
s: Good people may appear in rags outwardly while being spiritually devoted within. They have conceived love for God, contemplate beholding Him, depend on His provision, and care only for the true Master.

l: world, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XX .. Pauri XX
s: The world was created by God, who infused power into it and observes its losing and winning. Whatever comes into the world eventually departs, and every person's turn arrives.

l: love, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XX .. Pauri XX
s: God's love moves good people to weep, laugh, or remain silent. It leads them to care for nothing except the true Master.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXI .. Pauri XXI
s: Guru Angad teaches that true love is absorption in God rather than attachment to worldly things. Nanak says that judging good and bad in this worldly manner is not true love. Guru Angad also teaches that saluting while criticizing God's works is vain and prevents a person from obtaining a place in God's court. The Pauri urges remembrance and worship of the Lord, avoidance of evil deeds, and careful conduct to gain profit with the Lord.

l: Guru Angad, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXI .. Pauri XXI
s: Guru Angad teaches that true love is being ever absorbed in God rather than attached to worldly things. He also teaches that saluting while criticizing God's works is mistaken and vain.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXI .. Pauri XXI
s: Nanak says that a person who judges what is good as good and what is bad as bad in this manner is not a true lover. Nanak also says that such a person will not obtain a place in God's court.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXI .. Pauri XXI
s: God is the one in whom a true lover remains absorbed. God's works should not be criticized while being saluted, and a person should act carefully to gain profit with the Lord.

l: love, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXI .. Pauri XXI
s: Love that attaches itself to worldly things is not true love. True love is described as being ever absorbed in God.

l: evil deeds, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXI .. Pauri XXI
s: Evil deeds bring suffering. The text instructs a person to do absolutely nothing evil and to look well before acting.

l: worship, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXI .. Pauri XXI
s: Worship of the Lord is presented as a way to find happiness. The text urges remembrance of the Lord through worship.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Slok XXII, attributed to Guru Angad, teaches that a servant should efface himself, perform service faithfully, and avoid pride, quarrelsomeness, and excessive talk. It says that a person's heart reveals itself, that poison does not yield ambrosia, and that friendship with a fool is unprofitable and short-lived. It contrasts falsehood with the pleasure of praising God and says that supplication, not command, is appropriate toward God. Pauri XXII says that a servant who follows the master's wishes receives greater honour and double wages, while one who competes with the master loses his salary and is beaten.

l: Guru Angad, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Guru Angad is named as the speaker of the teachings in Slok XXII. He teaches about service, humility, speech, friendship, falsehood, and praising God.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Nanak says that the person who longs for God shall meet Him and that the longing will be acceptable. Nanak also says that pleasure lies in praising God and that commands will not succeed with Him.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: God is one whom the longing person shall meet. Commands do not succeed with God; He must be addressed through supplications or implored.

l: servant, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: The servant who is proud, quarrelsome, and talkative does not please the master. A servant who effaces himself and performs service obtains honour, while one who follows the master's wishes receives greater honour and double wages.

l: master, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: The master is displeased by a proud, quarrelsome, and talkative servant. A servant who vies with the master excites his jealousy, loses his large salary, and receives shoe-beating on the mouth.

l: service, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Service should be performed with humility and without pride, quarrelsomeness, or excessive talk. Faithful service according to the master's wishes brings honour and double wages.

l: longing for God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Longing for God leads the person who has it to meet Him. Nanak says that this longing is acceptable.

l: the fool, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: A fool acts according to his understanding, and friendship with a fool is not profitable. Whatever a fool does cannot be done well; even if he does one or two things well, he spoils the rest.

l: friendship, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Friendship with a fool is unprofitable. Friendship for a fool and love for a great man are compared to lines drawn on water, leaving neither trace nor mark.

l: praising God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Praising God is associated with pleasure. Nanak says that pleasure is found in praising God.

l: man, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: What a man has in his heart comes forth, so lip-worship is of no avail. A man who sows poison should not expect ambrosia, and a foolish man cannot perform his actions well.

l: Slok XXII, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Slok XXII contains teachings attributed to Guru Angad about humble service, the revelation of the heart, the futility of friendship with a fool, falsehood, supplication to God, and praising God.

l: Pauri XXII, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXII .. Pauri XXII
s: Pauri XXII teaches that a servant who acts according to the master's wishes receives honour and double wages. It warns that competing with the master brings jealousy, loss of salary, and shoe-beating, and concludes that God must be implored rather than commanded.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: Guru Angad teaches that a gift obtained through personal asking differs from the wonderful gift received when the Lord is pleased. He also teaches that true service is marked by absorption in the love of the master rather than freedom from fear. Nanak says that God's end and boundaries are unseen, and that God Himself creates and destroys. The unit says that God causes people to act, and that He who made the world takes care of it.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: Nanak says that the wonderful gift is obtained when the Lord is pleased. He says that a servant is absorbed in the love of the master and that God's end and boundaries are unseen. Nanak also says that God causes people to act and that the one who made the world takes care of it.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: God's end is not seen, nor does He have a thither or a hither side. He Himself creates and destroys, causes people to act, and acts Himself.

l: gift, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: A gift obtained by personal asking is contrasted with the wonderful gift obtained when the Lord is pleased.

l: service, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: Service in which the fear of the master does not depart is contrasted with service marked by absorption in the love of the master.

l: servant, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: A servant is called one who is absorbed in the love of the master.

l: love, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: Love of the master is the state in which a servant is absorbed.

l: creation, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: God Himself creates.

l: destruction, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: God Himself again destroys.

l: people (those with chains or horses), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: Some people have chains on their necks, while some ride on many horses. God causes them to act.

l: world, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: God made the world.

l: care, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIII .. Pauri XXIII
s: The one who made the world takes care of it.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIV .. Pauri XXIV
s: The unit concerns God’s creation, ordering, sustenance, and power over all beings. Guru Nanak teaches that God makes and fills vessels, determines their conditions, and regenerates those upon whom He looks with favour. Guru Angad states that God arranges all things and oversees the birth and death of animals. The Pauri declares that God’s greatness cannot be expressed, that man must do the work destined for him, and that God alone is the abiding Place.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIV .. Pauri XXIV
s: God makes and fills vessels, places what He has made in its proper place, and oversees the birth and death of animals. He provides creatures with sustenance, regenerates those upon whom He looks with favour, and does what He pleases.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIV .. Pauri XXIV
s: Guru Nanak teaches that God makes and fills vessels, gives different beings different conditions, and regenerates those upon whom He looks with favour. He also states that God does everything Himself and that there is no abiding Place except in God alone.

l: Guru Angad, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIV .. Pauri XXIV
s: Guru Angad teaches that God Himself arranges what He has made and puts it in its proper place. He says that God created animals and beholds their birth and death.

l: man, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok XXIV .. Pauri XXIV
s: Man must do the work that God destined for him from the beginning.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Sri Rag and Ashtapadi concern God, the Guru, God's name, truth, virtue, love, and the human condition. They teach that man gains happiness, honour, purity, and deliverance through the Guru, the Word, and devotion to God's name, while pride, mammon, counterfeit conduct, and attachment to worldly wealth lead to suffering and ruin. God's court is reached by those who are true, virtuous, and imbued with God's name. Nanak repeatedly declares that God alone is true, eternal, and the source of all gifts, while death overtakes all worldly bodies and possessions.

l: Sri Rag, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Sri Rag teaches that man should reject intoxicating illusion, counterfeit conduct, pride, and attachment to worldly adornments. It directs man toward truth, virtue, God's name, the Guru, and service to God as the means of happiness and honour in God's court.

l: Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Ashtapadi praises God's greatness and teaches that all are wives of the Spouse who must seek genuine love rather than hypocrisy. It explains that the Guru, the Word, God's name, truth, and love deliver man from pride, ritualism, worldly attachment, and the ocean of the world.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Nanak teaches that God alone is true and that man obtains happiness, honour, and deliverance through the Guru, the Word, and God's name. He declares that worldly wealth, ritual, pride, and bodily life cannot save man from death.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: God is described as the One Giver, True One, Creator, Spouse, Relisher, Enjoyer, and eternal Lord who pervades everything. God creates, destroys, gives, takes, assays people, bestows favour, and grants happiness, truth, and deliverance.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The Guru gives God's name, explains the Word, teaches truth, and leads man across the ocean of the world. The Guru is described as a ladder, boat, raft, lake, sea, and sacred stream, and as the means by which man meets God and becomes pure.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: God's name is the true merchandise, pure wealth, a jewel, and the support that brings happiness, honour, purity, and deliverance. Through the Guru, God's name removes sin, fear, pride, and transmigration.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The Word cleanses the heart and body, removes pride and desire, and gives truth, love, knowledge, and honour. Those imbued with the Word are delivered and remain united with God.

l: God's court, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: God's court is the place of honour, happiness, truth, and acceptance. Those who are false, counterfeit, impure, or separated from God are despised or denied entrance, while those imbued with God's name and the Word receive honour there.

l: woman, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The virtuous woman practices truth, loves her Spouse, obeys Him, and is decorated with the Guru's word and God's name. She is united with God, does not become a widow, and receives honour and happiness.

l: man, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Man is urged to serve God, meditate on God's name, practice truth and virtue, and take refuge in the Guru. Man is temporary, subject to death and transmigration, and cannot carry worldly possessions beyond this life.

l: mammon, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Mammon ruins the woman separated from her Spouse and leads man into pride, worldly love, wandering, and counterfeit conduct. Those under mammon fail to recognize that the real treasure is within and suffer in the ocean of the world.

l: truth, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Truth is the condition for pleasing God, entering God's court, and obtaining honour. The text teaches that truth is superior to all other practices and that the practice of truth purifies man.

l: virtue, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Virtue brings happiness, purity, and union with the Perfect One. Those who abandon evil under the Guru's instruction become absorbed in God, while those without virtue lose human life.

l: God's love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Love for God is compared with the lotus's love for water, the fish's need for water, the chatrik's longing for rain, water's protection of milk, and the chakwi's longing for the sun. Genuine love unites the separated with God and removes pride.

l: pride, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Pride makes the heart impure, causes man to wander in worldly attachment, and prevents spiritual understanding. The Guru's instruction and the Word remove pride.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Death overtakes man regardless of learning, rank, wealth, ritual, family, or worldly authority. The body returns to dust, and only God's name and God's favour provide deliverance.

l: the ocean of the world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The ocean of the world is fearful, dangerous, boundless, and without its own boat, raft, pole, or boatman. The true Guru ferries across it those upon whom the Guru looks with favour.

l: the intoxicant illusion, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The intoxicant illusion is given to man and causes him to forget death while enjoying temporary pleasure. It contrasts with the truth obtained by abstainers and with the lasting intoxication of God's name.

l: the boat, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The boat represents the means of crossing toward God and is identified with the Guru. The Guru is also called the ladder, raft, lake, sea, and sacred stream that carry man across the ocean of the world.

l: the counterfeit, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The counterfeit includes false merchandise, false conduct, false devotion, and hypocrisy. It is rejected from God's treasury, brings dishonour and transmigration, and cannot obtain God's court.

l: wealth, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Worldly wealth, including gold, silver, lands, animals, houses, authority, and possessions, does not accompany man after death and becomes an entangling net. God's name is identified as pure wealth that makes God man's friend.

l: the body, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The body is impure without the Word and is temporary, dependent on breath, and destined to return to dust. It cannot be preserved by adornment, ritual, wealth, or worldly pleasure.

l: the soul, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The soul suffers when separated from God and becomes entangled through pride, mammon, and counterfeit conduct. The Guru, the Word, and God's name bring the soul understanding, satisfaction, and deliverance.

l: the heart, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The heart is impure without the Word and becomes burdened by pride, worldly love, and desire. When God's name penetrates the heart, it receives happiness, truth, and freedom from disease.

l: the mind, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: The mind wanders under pride, mammon, worldly love, and false understanding. Through the Guru's instruction, the mind recognizes the world as a dream, becomes penetrated by God's name, and gains happiness.

l: religious ritual, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sri Rag .. Ashtapadi
s: Religious ritual, including penance, austerities, pilgrimage, alms, repeated ceremonies, prayer, reading, and bodily suffering, is insufficient without God, truth, and God's name. The text teaches that ritual without the Guru and the Word cannot remove sin, pride, or transmigration.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ghar III / Sri Rag ki War
s: Ghar III explains that Sat Sangat is known by the mention of the one God and that Duhagins are women separated from their husbands who forget their Spouse and wander unhonoured. It teaches that those pleased with God's will remove superstition from their minds. It identifies Nanak, the true Guru, by his association with every one. Sri Rag ki War presents faith, resignation, patience, divine judgment, and the unity of all creatures under God as central teachings.

l: Ghar III, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ghar III / Sri Rag ki War
s: Ghar III teaches how Sat Sangat and Duhagins are known. It says that those pleased with God's will remove superstition from their minds and that Nanak, the true Guru, is known by his association with every one.

l: Sat Sangat, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ghar III / Sri Rag ki War
s: Sat Sangat, the Society of the holy, is known by the mention of the name of the one God.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ghar III / Sri Rag ki War
s: God is the one shelter of all creatures. God may favor a crane over a swan and, if it pleases Him, change a raven into a swan; the perfect shall obtain a sight of God, while the fool shall find no place with Him.

l: God's will, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ghar III / Sri Rag ki War
s: Those who are pleased with God's will remove superstition from their minds.

l: Sri Rag ki War, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ghar III / Sri Rag ki War
s: Sri Rag ki War teaches that faith and resignation characterize the holy, while patience is the viaticum of angels. It says that all creatures have one shelter, that of God, and that divine favor can change how creatures are regarded.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: This unit concerns the Guru, Nanak, God, and the spiritual condition of human life in the world. It describes human aging, death, worldly impermanence, pride, sin, greed, and the folly of relying on external observances. It teaches that obedience to God's orders, meditation on God's Name, and the Guru's instruction lead toward truth, contentment, and God's court. Nanak, serving as a minstrel, sings the Word and receives the robe of true praise and the ambrosial food of the true Name.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: The Guru is the Giver, the house of snow, and the lamp of the three worlds. The Guru dispels pride, ends disputes, gives instruction, and provides the true goods that lead to God's court.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: Nanak teaches that the world is impermanent, that pride and external cleansing cannot remove inner sin, and that God's Name and the Guru's instruction bring happiness. He serves as a minstrel, singing the Word and receiving true praise and the ambrosial food of the true Name.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: God creates and separates body and soul, causes all things to happen, gives and removes power, and alone sustains all beings. God is the only enduring reality, and all beings depend on Him.

l: human life, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: Human life passes through stages of attachment, desire, household concerns, aging, weakness, and death. It is compared to a mansion of smoke, and its lasting value depends on remembering God and following the Guru's instruction.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: Death takes the soul from the body, while companions accompany the body to the pyre and relations offer food after death. Death overtakes rulers, possessions, bodies, and all worldly arrangements.

l: the ocean of the world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: The world is described as impermanent, deceptive, and subject to destruction. Its possessions, rulers, cities, pleasures, and beings cannot endure, while God alone flourishes.

l: pride, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: Pride causes people to claim what is not truly theirs and to suffer for their arrogance. When pride is dispelled through the Guru's instruction, a person meditates on God's Name and is accepted as genuine.

l: sin, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: Sin defiles a person inwardly even when the body and clothes are externally cleansed. The text says that sin is washed away through humility, God's Name, and the Guru's instruction.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: God's Name is to be remembered, repeated, and adored. Through the Name a person is absorbed in happiness, receives comfort, and approaches God's court.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: The Word regenerates those who humbly follow it and removes doubt from those to whom God gives it. Nanak sings the Word as true praise.

l: caste, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: Caste has no power in determining spiritual reality. What matters is obedience to God's order, which makes a person noble in God's court.

l: obedience to God's orders, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: Obedience to God's orders is sent into the world like a steed, while reflection on the Guru's instruction serves as its kettle-drums. Some people prepare for this journey and others set out upon it.

l: the fool, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: The fool mistakes possessions and pleasures for lasting goods, becomes involved in disputes, and fails to learn from instruction. What is said to the fool is lost, and the only way to establish friendship with him is to smite him on the mouth.

l: greed, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: Greed burns in the heart and causes the false to miss God's palace. The Guru's instruction quenches this fire.

l: the Guru's tree of contentment, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: The Guru's tree of contentment has religion as its blossom and divine knowledge as its fruit. It grows through good works and meditation, and its relish brings honour and the greatest gift.

l: the minstrel, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: The minstrel, once out of work, is appointed by God to sing His praises night and day. He is summoned to God's true court, clothed in a robe of true praise, and given the ambrosial food of the true Name.

l: the Perfect One, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Majh ki War
s: The Perfect One is obtained by those who utter true praise. Those who eat under the Guru's instruction gain satisfaction and comfort through Him.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The unit teaches that God, the Guru, the Name, and the Word deliver human beings from ignorance, pride, worldly desire, and death. It describes the soul and body, the body’s transience, and the soul’s immortality, while urging fear of God, truthful conduct, contentment, and meditation. Gauri Ashtapadi contrasts empty religious display and worldly power with devotion and Guru’s instruction. Gauri Chhant presents the bride’s longing for the Bridegroom and her fulfillment when united with Him through the Name and divine favor.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Nanak teaches that fear of God, the Guru, the Name, the Word, truth, and contentment lead to salvation and happiness. He says that worldly possessions, pride, learning without self-knowledge, and empty religious display are worthless.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: God is the compassionate and imperishable Lord who creates, preserves, destroys, and reanimates. God is contained everywhere and in every heart, grants the Name, protects human beings, and unites the bride with the Bridegroom.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The Guru is kind and merciful, reveals God, dispels doubt and ignorance, opens the understanding, and teaches the way to emancipation. Meeting the Guru enables people to recognize the Bridegroom and lose pride.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The Name is nectar, a support, and true wealth that frees human beings from worldly desires and death. Those who meditate on and repeat the Name are absorbed in God and obtain peace and happiness.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The Word is fashioned and decorated through fear of God and meditation. It saves those who follow the Guru’s instruction, while speech and writing without fear are worthless.

l: fear of God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Fear of God is weighty and necessary for salvation, love, and the destruction of fear of transmigration. It gives the Word its proper form and guards against empty understanding.

l: man, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The human being is born and absorbed according to the desires of the heart and is judged according to acts. Human life is precious but is wasted through sleep, eating, greed, pride, falsehood, and attachment to possessions.

l: the soul, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The soul does not die when spiritual ignorance and the body perish, because it is contained in the One who is everywhere. The soul is warned against supporting theft, slander, false witness, and other evil deeds.

l: the body, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The body is made of wind, water, and fire, has nine gates and a tenth door, and is ultimately reduced to ashes. It is described as temporary, burdened by worldly conduct, and unable to retain possessions after death.

l: the heart, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The mind is unstable when absorbed in lust, greed, pride, and worldly desire. Through the Guru’s instruction and meditation on the Name, it becomes fixed, pure, and free from wandering thoughts.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Death destroys bodies, kings, wealth, and created beings, and binds sinners in its city. Death cannot espy those whose hearts contain God’s true Name and who sing God’s praises.

l: Gauri Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Gauri Ashtapadi teaches that clothing, luxury, beauty, power, wealth, titles, and supernatural claims cannot bring happiness without God’s Name. It praises Guru’s instruction, humility, truth, and devotion as the means of knowing God.

l: Gauri Chhant, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Gauri Chhant portrays the bride’s painful longing for her absent Beloved and her joy when united with Him. It teaches that the Name, truth, contentment, Guru’s instruction, and God’s favor bring union, peace, and fulfillment.

l: the pious, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Saints and holy people are associated with the Name, truth, divine knowledge, and God’s love. Their minds are freed from filth, pride, and worldly entanglement, and they obtain happiness through God’s praises.

l: lust, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Lust is a worldly desire that ruins sinners when joined with wrath and draws human beings away from the Real Thing. Those absorbed in lust fail to recognize God’s essence.

l: wrath, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Wrath joins with lust and love for woman to ruin sinners. It is among the forces that assail and plunder the human being.

l: pride, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: Pride causes kings and religious figures to suffer, wander in transmigration, and remain subject to death. Through the Guru’s Word, pride is removed and supreme dignity is obtained.

l: woman, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The bride suffers sleepless longing and dishonor without her beloved Lord, and worldly ornaments, food, and pleasures cannot satisfy her. She becomes happy and fulfilled when she meets and unites with the Bridegroom through the Name and God’s favor.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri .. Gauri Chhant
s: The Bridegroom is recognized under the Guru’s instruction and comes home to the bride through divine favor. His union brings joy, peace, praise, and fulfillment of the bride’s desires.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Rag Asa teaches that God alone creates, sustains, judges, forgives, and grants truth, while caste, worldly status, ritual, wealth, and family attachment cannot secure spiritual benefit. It concerns man’s need to remember God’s Name, follow the Guru and the Guru’s instruction, abandon worldly love and mammon, and cultivate truth, devotion, mercy, contentment, and humility. Asa Ashtapadi continues that the Word and the true Name free people from sin, fear, transmigration, and death, while attachment, pride, greed, and false religious display bind them. Nanak repeatedly declares that God’s favour, the Guru’s guidance, and love of the Name lead to salvation and union with God.

l: Rag Asa, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Rag Asa teaches that God alone creates, sustains, judges, and grants truth. It urges man to abandon worldly attachment, empty ritual, pride, and reliance on status, and to seek God through the Guru, devotion, and the true Name.

l: Asa Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Asa Ashtapadi teaches that the Word and God’s Name bring peace, freedom from sin, protection from death, and union with God. It condemns worldly attachment, greed, pride, false learning, and religious display, and commends service to the Guru and meditation on the Name.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: God creates and sustains the universe, pervades all beings, and alone grants greatness, truth, forgiveness, contentment, mercy, and salvation. God looks favourably on some people, leads them to the Guru, removes their suffering and ignorance, and blends them with Himself.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Nanak teaches that God alone is the Spouse and Lord of all, and that worldly status, ritual, learning, wealth, and family attachment are fruitless without God’s Name. He declares that those who follow the Guru, abandon pride and worldly love, and meditate on the Name receive God’s favour and salvation.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: The Guru reveals God, teaches the true Name and the Word, removes doubt and suffering, and guides people across the dangerous ocean of the world. Service to the Guru brings peace, devotion, knowledge, freedom from entanglements, and union with God.

l: the True Guru's instruction, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: The Guru's instruction teaches people to remember the Name, reject greed, pride, falsehood, worldly love, and superstition, and practise truth, contentment, charity, and service. Through it, the mind is restrained, evil inclinations depart, and people are freed from transmigration and worldly entanglements.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: The true Name is the source of honour, purification, wisdom, devotion, and spiritual wealth. It blooms in the heart, destroys sin and fear, protects from death, and brings people to God’s court and salvation.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: The Word burns hopes and desires, brings the mind back from wandering, and reveals the True One. Whoever understands and continually meditates on the Word finds peace, happiness, and absorption in God.

l: worldly love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Worldly love binds people to family, possessions, desires, sin, and transmigration. It causes people to forget God’s Name, waste their human lives, and suffer, but it departs through God’s favour and the Guru’s instruction.

l: mammon, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Mammon represents the evil way of attachment to wealth, desire, and worldly possessions. Those who pursue mammon forget the Name, become greedy and proud, and are ultimately plundered and deprived of spiritual benefit.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Death threatens those who remain ignorant, attached, and without the Guru’s Word. Those who remember God’s Name, awaken in its love, and receive God’s favour are protected from the tortures and agents of death.

l: the mind, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: The mind is described as wandering, greedy, deceitful, proud, and attached to worldly love. Through the Guru’s instruction and the Word it can be restrained, purified, fixed on God, and brought to peace.

l: man, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Man is created and sustained by God, but suffers through ignorance, pride, worldly attachment, greed, and reliance on ritual or status. Man is accepted, forgiven, and saved by God’s favour when he follows the Guru, remembers the Name, practises truth and devotion, and abandons worldly love.

l: devotion, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Devotion consists in remembering and praising God, serving the Guru, accepting the Guru’s instruction, and practising truth, contentment, mercy, and faith. It enables people to cross the world’s dangerous ocean and obtain God’s favour and salvation.

l: truth, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Truth is granted by God and is learned through the Guru and the true Name. Practising truth and abandoning falsehood, greed, pride, and sin leads to God’s love, spiritual honour, and acceptance.

l: salvation, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: Salvation is obtained through God’s Name, the Guru’s guidance, devotion, and love of God. It frees people from worldly entanglements, sin, transmigration, fear, and death, and brings them into God’s presence.

l: true merchandise, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Asa .. Asa Ashtapadi
s: The Name as wealth is described as unfailing spiritual riches, including diamonds, jewels, rubies, and the pearl of the heart. Unlike worldly wealth, it accompanies and assists people after death, brings God’s favour, and leads to freedom and happiness.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: The unit concerns devotion to God, especially the young woman who seeks her Beloved through love, virtue, the true Word, and God's name. It teaches that God's favour brings happiness, spiritual companionship, and the ambrosial fruit, while sin, mammon, and worldly desire bring bitterness, anxiety, punishment, and death. Nanak urges the soul to remember God, seek the true Guru, and recognize divine knowledge. The unit also warns that without God's name and the true Word, beings wander in superstition and suffer separation.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: God is the Beloved and Spouse who mercifully delights in the devoted young woman, visits her, enjoys her companionship, and exchanges hearts with her. God grants favour, arranges human affairs, protects, and gives happiness and the ambrosial fruit through love, the true Word, and God's name.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: Nanak teaches that the young woman who sees God her Spouse is delighted and enraptured. He says that the soul must remember God, that those who lack God's name suffer, and that separated beings meet through the True Word.

l: woman, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: The young woman seeks the love of the one God, offers her soul and body to her Beloved, and finds happiness through the Word. When God favours her, she treasures the Word, sings a true song of rejoicing, and enjoys divine companionship.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: The true Word enables the devoted person to sing God's praises, obtain the ambrosial fruit, and remain connected with God. Those who receive it can meet after separation, while those without it wander and are punished on the road of death.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: God's name has infinite sweetness and value and brings happiness and protection from the bitterness of worldly desire. Without God's name, fools and the heedless wander in superstition, suffer, and are ruined.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: The true Guru gives knowledge of God and reveals divine knowledge to the person who thinks of him. The speaker inquires of the true Guru regarding the knowledge of God.

l: virtue, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: Virtue brings knowledge of God and abides with the person who embraces it. It drives vice away.

l: God's love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: Love of God brings companionship, happiness, and the fulfillment of the heart's desire. The person dyed with God's love prays to Him and exchanges hearts with Him.

l: sin, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: Sin appears sweet for only a short time, after which its fruit becomes bitter. The fruit of sin is compared to a fleeting wave of the ocean or flash of lightning.

l: mammon, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: Mammon is loved by the world and creates entanglement and mental anxiety. Its attraction is ultimately exposed and set aside.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: Death awaits the black deer, the bumble-bee, and the soul that becomes entangled in worldly desire. Without the Word, the person is bound and punished on the road of death.

l: the soul, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: The soul is described as coming from a strange land and becoming entangled in Death's net through worldly attachment. It is urged to serve God, dispel anxiety, and remember that rivers separated in their course may meet again only by chance.

l: happiness, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: Happiness comes to the wife whom God favours and to the person who offers soul and body to the Beloved. It is associated with God's name, the Word, love, and divine companionship.

l: divine knowledge, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Asa Chhant
s: Divine knowledge is learned through inquiry of the true Guru and through thinking of the true Guru. A rare person recognizes God through this knowledge.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: Rag Gujari teaches that true worship consists in meditating on the Name, cleansing the heart, performing good acts, and recognizing God as near and sustaining. It contrasts the benefits of devotion with the emptiness of ritual, arguing that the Name is necessary for purity, knowledge, peace, and deliverance. Gujari Ashtapadi presents prayers for love of the pure Name, describes worldly suffering and worldly love, and praises God's service under the guidance of the true Guru. It teaches that repeating God's name, receiving the Word, and seeking the true Guru's protection free people from pride, doubt, transmigration, avarice, and covetousness.

l: Rag Gujari, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: Rag Gujari teaches that the heart should be cleansed through the Name, good acts, and meditation on God. It says that ritual without the Name is futile, that God is near and caring, and that devotion leads toward purity and deliverance.

l: Gujari Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: Gujari Ashtapadi consists of prayers for love of God's pure Name and teachings on God's service, the true Guru, the Word, and freedom from worldly suffering. It says that repeating God's name and following the Guru's instruction bring divine knowledge, peace, stability, and release from transmigration.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: God is described as near, caring, infinite, unborn, and the support of the soul. God's light pervades the three worlds, and seeking God's name, service, protection, and favouring glance brings peace and deliverance.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: Nanak asks for the love of God's pure Name and for the nectar of the Name so that he may sing God's praises. He asks for protection, peace, freedom from avarice and covetousness, and God's Name as the capital of his heart.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: The Name is presented as essential to worship, purity, divine knowledge, peace, and deliverance. It is sought as wealth and capital for the heart, and repeating it frees people from worldly love, mourning, separation, disease, doubt, and transmigration.

l: devotion, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: Worship of God is performed by meditating on the Name, cleansing the heart, and mixing good acts with devotion. Without the Name, worship is said not to exist, while sincere devotion leads toward purity and deliverance.

l: God's service, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: God's service is described as the source of happiness and as something obtained through the favour of the Guru. Loving service, prayer, repeating God's name, and doing good works help a person cross the ocean of the world.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: The true Guru decides arguments, teaches God's name and service, and helps people overcome pride, worldly love, doubt, and transmigration. Seeking the true Guru's asylum stabilizes the mind and leads to divine meditation and purity of heart.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: The Word awakens those whose hearts contain light, and the Word of the true Guru enables a person to obtain the Pure God. Receiving the Guru's Word and teaching firmly implants God's name and service in the heart.

l: worldly love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: Worldly love intoxicates the mind and causes people to pursue wealth, while saturating them with the pain of birth and death. Being imbued with the Guru's Word and God's Name frees a person from worldly love.

l: transmigration, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Gujari .. Gujari Ashtapadi
s: Transmigration is associated with darkness, doubt, and the disease that ruins the world. Repeating God's name, seeking the true Guru's protection, and obtaining divine knowledge are presented as means of escaping it.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bihagre ki War
s: Bihagre ki War describes Hindus as having forgotten God and going in the wrong direction. It says they worship according to Narad’s instruction and characterizes them as blind, dumb, and ignorant fools. The unit says they take stones and worship them, questioning how a stone that sinks can carry them across.
